components.title: Process startup and main loop

components.title: Loading and thread services
components.summary: Provides main-thread identity, load and heartbeat threads, load locking, worker pools and platform thread support.

components.title: Synchronized simulation
components.summary: Owns frame-indexed units, features, commands, movement, resources, projectiles, weapons, LOS and deterministic event order.

components.title: Skirmish AI host and callbacks
components.summary: Loads AI libraries, delivers events, exposes the C callback table and translates commands into engine orders.

components.title: Unit command execution
components.summary: Validates network orders, invokes Lua command gates, queues commands and dispatches concrete unit behavior.

components.title: Builder and feature lifecycle
components.summary: Implements build, repair, guard, reclaim and resurrect targeting, feature mutation, deferred destruction and ID reuse.

components.title: Resource accounting
components.summary: Checks and applies per-action resource orders, accumulates unit production/use, and rolls team statistics and sharing windows.

components.title: Lua rules and projection boundary
components.summary: Hosts synced and unsynced Lua, control gates and lifecycle call-ins, with explicit synced-to-unsynced messaging.

components.title: Network and protocol
components.summary: Encodes, validates, distributes and consumes synchronized protocol messages including Skirmish AI commands.

components.title: Save, load and serialization
components.summary: Serializes the engine object graph and synced Lua state while delegating AI-private state through AI save/load events.

components.title: Rendering, UI and shipped content
components.summary: Owns unsynced presentation, UI frameworks, menu/controller surfaces and engine-distributed Lua/content assets.

components.title: Build, symbols, diagnostics and tests
components.summary: Defines binaries and build modes, extracts debug symbols, captures crashes, and provides unit and validation suites.

components.title: Documentation, packaging and automation
components.summary: Contains repository documentation, installer inputs, current container build definitions and automation workflows.

steps.description: Detect cores, register the main thread, construct SpringApp and call Run.
Install crash reporting, initialize, pump input and update the active controller.
Update jobs/network and consume network messages inside synchronized code.
Increment frame number and execute ordered AI, Lua and simulation updates.

flows.title: Skirmish AI command to unit command queue

steps.description: Translate C ABI command data to an internal Command and preserve its AI command ID.
Validate unit/team/order permission and send NETMSG_AICOMMAND.
Decode the synchronized AI command packet and rebuild the Command.
Validate player and team control and pass the order to the unit command AI.
Run AllowCommand and UnitCommand events, validate capability and dispatch concrete behavior.
Encode plain feature ID as MaxUnits plus feature ID in CMD_RECLAIM.
Decode feature-space ID, resolve current feature, and stop safely if absent.
Move into range and bind the builder reclaim target.
Store the target and create a reclaim death dependence.
Copy the target pointer, validate range/stance and apply negative build power.
Gate the step, account resources, reduce reclaimLeft and request deletion at completion.
Emit destruction events, clear the index and free the feature object.
Notify dependency listeners before detaching relationships.
Delay returning the ID while builder caches still report reclaim activity.
Compute reclaimed fraction, energy use and resource addition.
Record pull, check/scale the order and debit and credit resources.
Every 30 frames snapshot resource counters and run team sharing/statistics.
Install engine crash reporting after SpringApp construction.
If core dumps are disabled, replace handlers for fatal and control signals.
Log signal identity and attempt a symbolized halted stack trace.
Reset registered signals rather than restoring an earlier external handler.

facts.statement: A simulation frame increments frameNum, updates AI before the main simulation block, fires GameFrame before unit/feature updates, and fires GameFramePost after team/player updates.
The inspected AI update event is called synchronously from SimFrame through EngineOutHandler and SkirmishAIWrapper.
Skirmish AI callback wrappers and legacy callback state reside in fixed engine-owned arrays indexed by AI ID and are reset on release.
Skirmish AI feature access is a polling callback surface with plain feature IDs; absent IDs return sentinel/default values.
Internal reclaim commands distinguish a feature from a unit by encoding the target as MaxUnits plus featureId.
A Skirmish AI order is serialized to NETMSG_AICOMMAND and re-enters the synchronized simulation through ClientReadNet and AINetOrder.
Every admitted unit command passes through the event/Lua AllowCommand gate before concrete command execution.
ExecuteReclaim resolves the current feature by bounds-checked handler lookup and finishes the command if the feature is absent.
A builder registers a death dependence on its reclaim target, and target destruction clears the pointer and stops build activity.
UpdateReclaim copies curReclaim before AddBuildPower because that call can indirectly clear the member.
Completing feature reclaim marks the feature for deletion; the feature update phase later emits events, clears the indexed pointer and frees the object.
Deleted feature IDs are considered for reuse every 32 frames and remain withheld while builder caches report active reclaim.
Feature reclaim computes a bounded resource order and mutates reclaimLeft only after IssueResourceOrder succeeds.
Team pull/income/expense windows, sharing and statistics roll every 30 simulation frames.
CREG save state includes units, features, projectiles, teams, command descriptions, Skirmish AI host state and synced Lua state.
With core dumps disabled, SpringApp installs Recoil fatal-signal handlers after construction and the Linux installer does not preserve prior handlers in the shown calls.
A constructor-time external signal tracer can be replaced later by Recoil's CrashHandler::Install when core dumps are disabled.

The current native diagnostic reportedly completed ReclaimFeature and later submitted ReclaimArea before a crash between its NativeAdmission and dispatch markers; no retained native backtrace identifies the failing engine path.
The available source and reported markers do not establish a ReclaimFeature-specific or ReclaimArea-specific crash cause.
The default CMake build type is RelWithDebInfo, and the Docker build configuration uses optimized code with debug information for that mode.
The indexed test tree contains no focused test for the complete Skirmish AI feature-reclaim network-to-feature-deletion flow.

open_questions: Which signal, instruction pointer, native thread and loaded module own the reported crash?
Did the failure occur before ClientReadNet, during packet decoding, in Lua AllowCommand, while queueing, or during a later builder slow update?
Which exact command occupied the builder queue head at failure time?
Were core dumps enabled, and which component last installed each fatal-signal handler?
Was the Skirmish AI callback still active with the same AI and team identity?
Did Lua delete or mutate a unit or feature during AllowCommand or AllowFeatureBuildStep?
Can a symbol-matched RelWithDebInfo build reproduce with a retained core or a post-install diagnostic handler?
